topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It sets out the lecture themes on cancer evolution, the tumor microenvironment, and the intended learning outcomes.

topics.label: Genetic and epigenetic drivers of clonal evolution
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutational clonal selection and epigenetic alterations confer competitive growth advantages during tumor initiation and progression.

topics.label: Cancer stem cells and cell of origin
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the cancer stem cell model and present experimental evidence for cell-of-origin hierarchies in leukemia and colorectal cancer.

topics.label: Microenvironmental promotion and stromal dependency in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how inflammatory signals, environmental promoters, and supportive stroma create permissive conditions required for malignant outgrowth.

topics.label: Methods for investigating tumor evolution
topics.groupedBecause: It details the experimental, single-cell, and spatial omics technologies used to map tumor heterogeneity and microenvironmental interactions.

topics.label: Multifactorial synthesis of cancer evolution
topics.groupedBecause: It integrates genetic, epigenetic, cell-of-origin, and microenvironmental factors into a unified evolutionary model of cancer development.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next session preview
topics.groupedBecause: It provides closing remarks for the lecture and previews the upcoming session on cancer therapies.
